problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1 \\ 6 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Volume of an N-Dimensional Parallelepiped
examples.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043085/assets/47850d3c530a29de8cb5df4bb3e035b9e29fb1ba65ff0eca2d39e6d8e0a2b06b.png)
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $\mathbf{a},$ $\mathbf{b},$ $\mathbf{c},$ and  $\mathbf{d}{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043085/assets/0563d565dff1928d21da21ad832fad37f94fb385ddb8a805423ae2577ae9434c.png)

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M{:}$

$$
V = | \det(M) |
$$

Notice that the $2$nd row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $2$nd row of the $3 \times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot 1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(15+4) \\  & =-57.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V = | \det(M) | = |-57| = 57.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$H=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the $3$rd row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $1$st row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-6-0) \\  & =3\cdot (-6) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$
